items.headline: Apple rebuilds Siri on a licensed Google Gemini model at WWDC
items.diff_narrative: No antecedent on 2026-06-07, where the Siri overhaul existed only as a WWDC expectation folded into the events bullet (chatbot-style assistant with on-screen awareness and personal context). Today it lands as confirmed news from the Monday June 8 keynote: Apple's rebuilt Siri is powered by a custom ~1.2-trillion-parameter Google Gemini mixture-of-experts model (internally 'Apple Foundation Models v10'), under a multi-year deal reported around $1 billion a year, with analyst estimates of total value up to $5 billion. New today are the concrete topology (a ~3B on-device model, heavier requests to Apple Silicon under Private Cloud Compute with PII stripped before reaching the Gemini layer), the user-visible surface (dedicated Siri app, system-wide 'Search or Ask' gesture, Dynamic Island, multi-step cross-app actions), and the OS ship schedule (iOS/iPadOS/macOS/watchOS/tvOS/visionOS 27 developer betas now, public betas in July, general release in fall). This is a state-change from speculation to a confirmed strategic concession of the assistant's core to a rival.

items.headline: WWDC opens a model-agnostic agent surface (App Intents + Foundation Models + user-selectable assistant)
items.diff_narrative: Not present in any form on 2026-06-07. Today's keynote adds the developer-facing half of the Apple story: an Extensions mechanism lets users choose which assistant answers the 'Search or Ask' panel - Siri, Google Gemini, or ChatGPT, with Apple confirmed to have tested Anthropic's Claude - making the system assistant a model-agnostic slot for the first time. Deeper App Intents integration is the mechanism by which the new assistant chains tasks across third-party apps, and the Foundation Models framework exposes the on-device model to developers for tool-calling and guided (structured) generation with no per-call charge. The net new framing: the largest consumer device base is becoming an addressable agent surface in two directions (apps expose intents an assistant can orchestrate; apps call a free on-device LLM). Detailed API sessions run June 9-12, so entitlement and tool-permission specifics are still open.

items.headline: AI events to plan around now (three-track calendar)
items.diff_narrative: Carries forward from 2026-06-07's events bullet, with the key shift being WWDC's status: yesterday it 'opens this coming Monday June 8' with the 10:00 AM PT keynote still ahead; today it is underway, having opened June 8 and running through June 12, now anchored on the in-progress Siri and Foundation Models sessions rather than a pending keynote. The rest of the calendar is largely stable: Databricks Data + AI Summit (June 15-18, Moscone), AI Engineer World's Fair (June 28-July 2, Moscone West, 29 tracks), Confidential Computing Summit (June 23-24, SF Mint), SecurityWeek AI Risk Summit (Aug 11-12, Half Moon Bay), AMD Advancing AI (July, MI400/MI455X), Hot Chips (Stanford, Aug 23-25), AI Infra Summit (Sept 15-17, Santa Clara), GitHub Universe (Oct 28-29) and AWS re:Invent (Nov 30-Dec 4) all persist. Minor adjustments today: the AI Engineer World's Fair track description gains explicit inference and security tracks; Black Hat USA's AI Summit is now specified as a single-day Aug 4 event inside the Aug 1-6 conference (yesterday listed Black Hat as Aug 1-6 and gave DEF CON 34's AI Village explicit Aug 6-9 dates); the Confidential Computing Summit speaker line is generalized to NVIDIA, AMD, Google, Microsoft and Meta (yesterday highlighted a specific NVIDIA attestation session). Citations for several events also rotated (Macworld replaced by Gadgetbridge for WWDC, PR Newswire replaces Linux Foundation for the Confidential Computing Summit, AMD CES newsroom replaces Wccftech, Moscone added for the AI Engineer World's Fair).

items.headline: Yesterday's leads (BYD humanoid, Broadcom chip sell-off, DeployBench) not repeated today
items.diff_narrative: For a reader tracking the diff: the three other 2026-06-07 leads produced no fresh state-change on 2026-06-08 and so are intentionally not carried forward. BYD's humanoid-robot confirmation was a June 3-4 disclosure with no new development today; the Broadcom-led semiconductor sell-off was a multi-day market move (June 4-5) with no new trading-session escalation reported today; and DeployBench (arxiv 2606.05238) was a one-time benchmark publication with no follow-on. Their absence reflects the no-inertia rule (a storyline must have a new event to be repeated), not a reversal or correction of yesterday's reporting.
